title: Kepler Q11 to Q17 give a weak second-harmonic test of the 19.48-hour KIC 10001893 signal
abstract: We test the waveform of the known 19.48-hour signal of KIC 10001893 in 14 Kepler release 25 quarters. We fix the frequency and phase from earlier work and early aperture flux. Joint fits include a fundamental, a second harmonic, local lines and a strong pulsation. Later aperture flux gives a phase-aligned second harmonic of 2.26 +/- 5.75 parts per million with 6-day noise blocks. An ideal Lambert sphere viewed edge-on predicts 3.99 parts per million from the measured fundamental. The prediction is below one standard error. Corrected flux and instrument fits also have weak sensitivity. These data do not select reflection or a sinusoidal light response. The test is conditional on the fixed frequency, phase and noise model. No planet or new signal is confirmed. Code, source hashes, aggregate results and retrieval steps are supplied.

display.caption: Later phase-aligned second harmonic with conditional normal intervals. Diamonds show an ideal edge-on Lambert prediction. Products share observations.
